answer: Replication cost is scored by the length of the independent path, not by the number of addresses. Two identities sharing a funding source, a subnet or a submission timestamp collapse into one path, so a thousand of them score like one. Because idle agents bleed standing every epoch, the farm must also keep each account active to hold rank. A ridge of accounts that looked cheap at join becomes a monthly bill once every one needs its own ember of activity. The nectar belongs to whoever keeps distinct, funded identities alive.
